text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] GPU capacity alarm fired for eu-west pool — queued requests > 20k, request throttle at 95%.

alice: oncall-2 picking up. quick status please — what's the customer impact?

support-oncall: partial outages and timeouts on generation endpoints for EU customers, spike started ~00:05 UTC. SLO alerts firing.

bob: looking at autoscaler logs: repeated failures with `scale_limit_reached` and `insufficient_quota`. controller kept hitting `max_pool_size`.

carol: confirmed. queue grew after an internal batch churned nodes. trying to find the batch job owner now.

dkim: i'll attempt manual scale up of eu-west pool by +8 GPUs to provide headroom.

alice: go for it. also start routing non-prod traffic away and enable fallback to smaller model variants. notify router team.

sre-lead: running manual command to add capacity:
```
# add 8 GPUs to eu-west reserved pool
rctl pool resize --pool eu-west-gpu --add 8 --reason "incident manual scale"
```

sre-lead: command accepted, provisioning started, new_target=32.

bob: autoscaler controller indicates cooldown flapping plus an explicit safety cap `max_pool_size=24` — that's why it wouldn't scale automatically.

carol: can we temporarily bump `max_pool_size`? need to know risk/rollback plan.

alice: approved for emergency bump. ephemeral change, auto-revert after 30m. carol/bob coordinate.

bob: applying ephemeral bump now:
```
rctl pool update eu-west-gpu --set max_pool_size=40 --ephemeral true
```

bob: new max applied; controller scheduled desired=36, provisioning underway.

support-oncall: router rule applied: divert 20% traffic to us-west and send low-priority requests to CPU fallback. updating status page.

dkim: pausing internal recurring batch that started at 00:05 UTC to stop further queue pressure.

carol: identified top tenant generating heavy load: tenant-9243 running massive batched evals on high-context model. emailing SE and applying throttle.

alice: apply emergency tenant throttle 80% and reduce their concurrency.

carol: applied `tenant.9243.rate=0.2` (temporary). monitoring queue impact.

sre-lead: queue depth trending down: 21k -> 6k within ~12 minutes. CPU fallback carrying ~15% of requests.

bob: posting recent controller logs for context:
```
[2077654325] controller: desired=36 current=24 provisioning=12
[2077654370] node-provisioner: instance i-0a3f... created
[2077654430] runtime: kv-cache warmup complete
```

support-oncall: status page updated: Partial degradation for EU generation endpoints; mitigation in progress — https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2077654321

alice: immediate action checklist:
- monitor until queue < 500
- ephemeral `max_pool_size` auto-revert in 30m
- draft postmortem: root cause + timeline + customer impact
- action items: prevent large internal batches during peak, add emergency pool escrow, improve autoscaler visibility/alerts

dkim: creating runbook ticket and tagging infra PRs for follow-up.

carol: i'll draft the postmortem including timeline and customer-facing summary; will include log snippets and metrics.

alice: any blockers left?

bob: nodes are healthy and joining runtime. no further immediate blockers. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT PARTIAL RESOLVE: queue depth < 500, throttles active, ephemeral capacity scheduled to auto-revert in 30m. Channel open for 1h for follow-ups.

support-oncall: updating affected tickets and sending mitigation email to customers.

alice: great work everyone. follow-up action: autoscaler should emit explicit `max_pool_size_blocking` alert so ops don't mistake saturation for other failures. add to infra backlog.

carol: noted — adding to postmortem actions. closing thread in 1h unless more issues appear. :white_check_mark:
